premise: I poured my $129,000 nursing pension into launching a specialized memory‑care day center with my stepdaughter, who notarized a 50% stake and guaranteed free daily care for my mother; when a senior‑living chain bid $940,000 for the license and client list, she forged a dissolution, sold my share, and handed me a $5,200 “respite” check—I discovered the partnership documents locked inside a false‑bottomed file cabinet, voided the sale, and now operate “Memory of Deceit Care,” where she folds linens in a smock that says “Forgotten Trust” and every intake form prints the perjury‑docket number.
